text:
rachel: quick flag - after the recent packaging change a customer using Deno Deploy + Bun hit ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED and TS/VSCode didn't pick up types in their mono-repo sample. Repro below. :confused:

pete: can you paste the minimal import and package.json?

rachel: import in their worker: 
```js
import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference';
const c = createClient({ apiKey: Deno.env.get('REDWOOD_KEY') });
await c.predict('hi');
```
error: `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED: Package subpath './lib/index.js' is not defined by "exports"`
package.json (snippet): 
```json
{"name":"redwood-inference","version":"5.0.0","main":"lib/index.cjs","exports":{"./lib/index.js":"./lib/index.cjs"},"types":"lib/index.d.ts"}
```

lucy: interesting - this is slightly different from the Vercel/Cloudflare threads. Deno and Bun are more eager about ESM and will try to resolve `./lib/index.js`/`./lib/index.mjs`. Because exports only maps that to a CJS file, the resolver fails. Also, some editors (VSCode with TS server) will not resolve types when the exports map doesn't expose a types path or root entry.

den0-bot: (typo alert) deno-bot: Deno runtime uses strict ESM resolution; packages should provide an `import` condition or an actual ESM file.

pete: For a quick local test I swapped exports to a more explicit mapping: 
```json
{"exports":{
  ".": {"import":"./lib/index.mjs","require":"./lib/index.cjs","types":"./lib/index.d.ts"},
  "./package.json":"./package.json"
}}
```
That fixed the Deno repro and restored editor typings for me.

rachel: thanks. The odd part: some customers still reported no intellisense after adding top-level "types". Is that expected?

lucy: yeah, TS resolution is weird: when an exports map exists, TS uses export subpath resolution for both JS module resolution and declaration lookup. If the consumer resolves '.' to an export subpath that doesn't include a `types` field, TS server may not find the declarations. Best practice is to include a `types` entry in the `.` export and keep the top-level `types` fallback to be safe.

den0-bot: deno-bot: Bun also reads the package.json and prefers ESM entries; bundlers like esbuild will look for import conditions. Exposing only CJS is a cross-runtime footgun.

pete: alternative approach if building a full ESM bundle is costly: publish a tiny ESM entry file `lib/index.mjs` that re-exports the public API (either built ESM or a thin wrapper doing dynamic import of CJS). Then map import->lib/index.mjs in exports. That satisfies Deno/Bun and modern bundlers.

rachel: action plan suggestion: 
- revert the recent export-only-CJS change and cut a patch release ASAP (P0)
- publish follow-up that adds dual export entries (import/require) + types on the root export + ./package.json subpath (P0)
- add packaging CI matrix that runs sample apps on Deno Deploy, Bun, Vercel Edge emulator, and Cloudflare Pages preview for PRs touching package.json/exports (P1)
- docs: short KB on "how export maps affect edge/deno/bun + TS" with sample package.json shapes and recommended workarounds (P2)

lucy: agree. Also add a small test in our sample-apps repo that imports the package the same way customers do (from package root) and runs a lightweight runtime check on the supported platforms. Would have caught this earlier.

pete: short-term support workaround to give customers: 
- import explicit ESM path (`import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference/lib/index.mjs'`) or 
- pin to last working patch release.

rachel: i'll open an issue with the customer repro and attach zips. pete, can you draft the revert PR? i'll coordinate with releases to push the patch once CI is green.

infra-bot: CI job created: packaging-smoke-matrix (node18/node20/deno/bun/vercel-emulator/cloudflare-preview).

rachel: thanks all. ping me on the PR and i'll validate the Vercel/Deno previews once the patch is built. :thumbsup:
